summary: The marketing team is doubling down on Asia Star and the new Intelligent China program as its top promotional priorities, while finalizing the Knowledge website redesign and urgently driving traffic to the newly launched Intelligent China webpage.
summaryDetail: The biggest push right now is the Intelligent China program: its webpage launched this week and the team must immediately drive traffic to it, with audience profiles for Asia Star and CRM hot leads also due. The Knowledge website redesign is in its final stretch—Joseph, Julie, and the team lead need a 30-minute working session to mark specific feedback before Joker revises the design, and Joseph must share the HTML inspiration file. On the paid media front, Joseph is drafting a plan for target areas, audience focus, and search prompts, while the team audits the Google Ads conversion tracking setup to ensure accurate measurement. Meanwhile, a lingering Outlook account lockout from stale saved passwords has kept the team troubleshooting across devices, and the CKGSB–EuroCham Shanghai event on November 13 has been cancelled, freeing up focus for the core China-based programs.

decisions.text: Stale saved passwords across devices caused the account lockout; all devices must update credentials.
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic instead
Keep the two-menu structure with School menu at top and Knowledge menu centered
Bring the BCI/BSI indices banner into the Knowledge section
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the very top of the homepage
Use card types to visually distinguish content types (professor, article, etc.)
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs for promotion.
Treat US partner programs (Stanford, Columbia) as secondary; consider Berkeley as a possible third priority.
Put US partnerships on hold for the first quarter to focus on China-based programs.
Cancel the CKGSB–EuroCham Shanghai event scheduled for November 13
